claims.statement: The metrics prerequisite requires enabled Copilot usage-metrics policy with enterprise/organization policy references. A dashboard link or subscription does not prove effective enablement or viewing permission.

The short account note says an active Pro, Pro+ or Max personal plan is automatically canceled after assignment of a Business or Enterprise seat. It is conditional on seat assignment, not a cancellation action performed here.

The full account note adds a prorated refund for the unused current personal cycle and continued use governed by company policies. No actual refund, cancellation or entitlement was verified; the short fragment must not be assumed to independently state these extra terms.

The access prerequisite says Copilot access is needed and links access guidance without specifying a particular paid plan. Its filename cannot turn this text into a paid-subscription-only requirement.

The telemetry note says metrics primarily reflect supported IDE activity with server telemetry supplementing active users, while website chat, mobile, code review and CLI are excluded from dashboard data. Such metrics cannot represent complete all-surface usage or inactivity.

The skill creation fragment requires a per-skill directory and exactly named SKILL.md with YAML required lowercase hyphenated unique name and description, optional license and Markdown instructions. Directory-name matching is described as typical rather than universal; license metadata is not rights clearance.

The skills fragment separates project locations .github/skills, .claude/skills and .agents/skills from personal locations under .copilot/skills or .agents/skills in the home directory. Optional resources and scripts are discoverable on invocation, not automatically safe or approved to execute.

The workflow-debugging example outlines run lookup, summarized then detailed failure logs, attempted reproduction and repair verification. It is imported illustrative instruction content, not instructions executed or evidence any failure was fixed.

The script section allows optional allowed-tools preapproval and states unlisted tools prompt for permission. Its warning says shell/bash preapproval removes terminal confirmation and can enable attacker-controlled skills or prompt injection to execute arbitrary commands; trusted review of the skill and scripts is essential, not file-existence attestation.

The script and skill-import examples describe relative-base execution, downloading/unpacking and moving skill directories, plus gh skill management capabilities. No example scripts, installs, publishing or preapproval occurred; imported skills remain untrusted evidence.
